review_evidence: Focused schema, runtime hash, pedagogy quality, and key self-review for eng_c3_ch08 on 2026-07-12
title: Thank God!
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Choose the lighter gift
levels.teaching_goal: Understand why a character chooses one fruit over another by using journey and weight clues.

guided_check.teaching_block: In this story, a farmer wants to carry a fruit gift over a long distance. Grapes and watermelons are both good fruits, but the lighter fruit is easier to carry.
guided_check.passage: The farmer has sweet grapes and large watermelons. The palace is far away, so he chooses the fruit that is easier to carry.
guided_check.prompt: Which fruit does the farmer choose for the journey?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: compare weight. A basket of grapes is lighter than a heavy watermelon.
bridge.passage: The farmer leaves the heavy fruit at home and carries the lighter fruit.
bridge.prompt: Which fruit is lighter to carry?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: a reason answer needs both the choice and the reason. He chose grapes because grapes were light.
masterclass.passage: The road is long. The farmer must carry the gift by hand.
masterclass.prompt: Which answer gives the clearest reason?

independent_check.teaching_block: Compare a new pair of choices and explain how the journey changes the sensible decision.
independent_check.passage: Farah must walk to a hilltop picnic. She can carry a clay water pot or a light steel bottle. Both hold enough water.
independent_check.prompt: Which container should Farah choose, and why?

concept_slots.description: Explains that it is lighter or easier to carry on the walk.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer practical comparison to a school task. Use both the load and the distance in the reason.
transfer_check.passage: The art room is upstairs. Neha can take one large glass jar or six empty paper cups to hold paintbrushes.
transfer_check.prompt: What should Neha carry upstairs, and why?

concept_slots.description: Explains that they are light, easier, or safer to carry upstairs.

levels.title: Understand the joke
levels.teaching_goal: Infer why the farmer is thankful when a small grape hits him.

guided_check.teaching_block: The funny turn in this story depends on comparison. A grape is small. A watermelon is heavy. The farmer feels lucky that he brought the smaller fruit.
guided_check.passage: The playful king tosses grapes. The farmer thinks about the heavy fruit he did not bring.
guided_check.prompt: Which fruit would have hurt much more?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: ask which fruit is heavier. A heavy fruit would hurt more if thrown.
bridge.passage: A grape taps the farmer lightly. He imagines a much heavier fruit instead.
bridge.prompt: Which fruit is the farmer glad he did not bring?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: the answer should explain the farmer's thinking. He thanks God because watermelons would hurt more than grapes.
masterclass.passage: The farmer smiles after the grape hits him because he imagines a heavy watermelon being thrown.

independent_check.teaching_block: Find the contrast that creates a funny lucky escape, then explain the character's reaction.
independent_check.passage: A coconut drops beside Ravi's foot. Ravi looks at the tiny seedpod that actually landed on his shoe and laughs with relief.

concept_slots.description: Mentions that only the tiny seedpod landed on his shoe.
Explains that the coconut would have hurt more.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use contrast to explain humour in a new everyday scene. State what happened and the worse possibility avoided.
transfer_check.passage: During cleanup, one drop of blue paint lands on Manu's old apron. The full paint jar had nearly fallen on his white uniform.
transfer_check.prompt: Why does Manu smile at the small stain?

concept_slots.description: Mentions the small stain on the old apron.
Explains that the full jar could have stained the white uniform.

levels.title: Use opposite words
levels.teaching_goal: Use common opposite pairs such as heavy/light and long/short.

guided_check.teaching_block: Opposite words show contrast. Heavy and light are opposites; long and short are opposites.
guided_check.passage: A watermelon is heavy. A grape is light.
guided_check.prompt: What is the opposite of heavy?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: think of what is easier to lift. Easy to lift means light.
bridge.passage: The bag is not heavy. It is easy to lift.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: use the pair. Heavy/light is about weight. Long/short is about length or distance.
masterclass.passage: The palace journey is long, but the walk to the tree is not long.
masterclass.prompt: What is the opposite of long?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now write the opposite without hints.
independent_check.passage: A long road takes more time. A short road takes less time.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use an opposite pair in a weather report rather than a food comparison. Keep the meaning category the same.
transfer_check.passage: The morning wind was gentle, but by afternoon it became strong.
transfer_check.prompt: Write the opposite of gentle from the passage.

levels.title: Choose is or are
levels.teaching_goal: Use is for one person or thing and are for more than one.

guided_check.teaching_block: Use is when the naming word is one. Use are when the naming word means more than one.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: these grapes means many grapes, so use are.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: one table is. Many tables are. One book is. Many books are.

independent_check.teaching_block: Use subject number to build a complete new sentence, not just fill one blank.
independent_check.passage: Subject: the green melon. Detail: heavy. Place: beside the basket.
independent_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence using is.

concept_slots.description: Uses is with the singular subject.
Gives its place beside the basket.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer singular-plural agreement to classroom objects and write the whole sentence clearly.
transfer_check.passage: Subject: the new maps. Detail: colourful. Place: on the back wall.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence using are.

concept_slots.description: Uses are with the plural subject.
Gives their place on the back wall.

levels.title: Order salad steps
levels.teaching_goal: Use sequence words to order steps in making a simple fruit salad.

guided_check.teaching_block: A recipe or making activity must happen in order. First starts the process; finally ends it.
guided_check.passage: First, take banana slices. Next, add papaya cubes. Finally, squeeze lemon juice.
guided_check.prompt: Which word tells the starting step?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: the first step comes before all other actions.
bridge.passage: First, wash the fruit. Then, cut it. Finally, mix it.
bridge.prompt: Which word marks the first action?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: sequence words are signals. First begins, next continues, then continues, finally closes.
masterclass.passage: First add banana. Next add grapes. Then mix. Finally add salt.
masterclass.prompt: Which word should introduce the last step?

independent_check.teaching_block: Turn an unseen recipe note into ordered instructions. Keep preparation before mixing and serving.
independent_check.passage: Steps: peel the banana / slice it / mix it with curd / serve in two bowls.
independent_check.prompt: Write the steps in order using sequence words.

concept_slots.description: Places mixing with curd after slicing.
Ends by serving in two bowls.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use ordered instruction writing for a hygiene routine instead of food preparation. Include every action once.
transfer_check.passage: Routine: wet your hands / rub with soap / rinse well / dry with a clean towel.
transfer_check.prompt: Write the routine in order using first, next, then, and finally.

concept_slots.description: Then tells the reader to rub with soap.
Ends with drying using a clean towel.

items.passage: A porter can carry either one heavy trunk or two light cloth bags up a steep path. Both choices hold the same supplies.
items.prompt: Which choice is easier, and why?

concept_slots.description: Explains that they are lighter or easier on the steep path.

items.passage: For a long bus ride, Keshav chooses a small box of dates instead of a large pot of soup.
items.prompt: Which reason best supports his choice?
options: the dates are easier to carry without spilling
the bus ride is very short
dates are heavier than a pot
accepted_answers: the dates are easier to carry without spilling

items.passage: A pebble taps Noor's helmet just after a brick slides to the ground behind her. Noor laughs with relief.
items.prompt: Why does Noor feel lucky?

concept_slots.description: Mentions the pebble or helmet tap.
Explains that the brick could have hit or hurt her more.

items.passage: One grape bounces off the farmer's cap. He remembers the heavy melons left at home and starts laughing.
items.prompt: What is the main idea of this moment?
options: the farmer feels lucky that the lighter fruit was thrown
the farmer wants a new cap
the grapes are heavier than melons
accepted_answers: the farmer feels lucky that the lighter fruit was thrown
he is glad it was a grape

items.passage: Mina complains about a tiny scratch until she sees that her bicycle stopped just before a deep ditch.
items.prompt: Which idea best sums up the scene?
options: a small problem can seem lucky beside a worse one
accepted_answers: a small problem can seem lucky beside a worse one
the small scratch was better than falling

items.passage: The empty basket is light; the basket filled with pumpkins is ___.
items.prompt: Choose the opposite of light.

items.passage: The first path is narrow, but the second path is ___.
items.prompt: Write the opposite of narrow.

items.passage: The mangoes ___ ripe.
items.prompt: Choose the correct word.

items.passage: The basket ___ beside the gate.
items.prompt: Write is or are.

items.passage: Subject: three red apples. Detail: fresh. Place: in the lunch box.
items.prompt: Turn the plural notes into one complete sentence with are.

concept_slots.description: Gives their place in the lunch box.

items.passage: Subject: one clay cup. Detail: empty. Place: near the tap.
items.prompt: Turn the singular notes into one complete sentence with is.

concept_slots.description: Gives its place near the tap.

items.passage: Steps: wash the guava / cut it into pieces / sprinkle salt.
items.prompt: Which action comes immediately before sprinkling salt?

items.passage: Words: finally / the / juice / pour / into / glasses
items.prompt: Put the words in order.
accepted_answers: finally pour the juice into glasses
finally, pour the juice into glasses.
pour the juice into glasses finally
pour the juice into glasses finally.

items.passage: Recipe plan: grate one carrot / add curd / stir well / serve cold.
items.prompt: Write the recipe in order using sequence words.

items.passage: The farmer carries a covered basket because dusty wind blows across the road.
items.prompt: Why is the basket covered?

concept_slots.description: Mentions covering or protecting the basket.
Explains that the cover keeps dust off the fruit.

items.passage: The host gives children small fruit bowls instead of one deep glass dish during an outdoor picnic.
items.prompt: Give a practical reason for the choice.

concept_slots.description: Gives a sensible sharing, carrying, or safety reason.

items.passage: The road to the orchard is rough, while the path beside the canal is smooth.
items.prompt: Which opposite pair appears?

items.passage: A boy ducks when a soft leaf brushes his cap, then notices a heavy branch has fallen behind him.
items.prompt: Explain why the leaf now seems lucky.

concept_slots.description: Mentions that only the soft leaf touched him.
Explains that the heavy branch could have hit or hurt him.

items.passage: Routine: open the lunch mat / place the plates / share the food / clean the area.
items.prompt: Write the routine in order.

items.passage: One crate is heavy. The empty bags ___ light.
items.prompt: Write the word that agrees with bags.
